items.claim: The row's sole named cohesion driver is tier-falsified: the 7:2 form reaches byte tier only at 7:2 and merely skeleton tier at 7:4, so 'recurs verbatim' and 'byte-verified at both' are both false.
items.evidence: All four quoted runs re-collate to BYTE tier at their own cited refs. But the bracket claim is a cross-ref claim, and re-collated cross-ref it fails: the quoted 7:2 form “בֵּֽית אֵ֗בֶל” reaches BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.7.2 and only SKELETON tier against oshb:Eccl.7.4. MT 7:4 reads “בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל” -- a prefixed-bet construct with different pointing and a different accent. At word-bound token level MT 7:2 carries “בית” while MT 7:4 carries “בבית”, so the only shared word-bound token is “אבל”; the phrase match is a contiguous consonantal substring, not a verbatim repeat. The boundary_rationale's 'identical phrase ... recurs verbatim at the cluster's close' and the device_notes' 'byte tier, byte-verified at both oshb:Eccl.7.2 and oshb:Eccl.7.4' therefore both overclaim the tier of the row's ONLY cohesion driver, which the row itself calls 'byte-named cohesion, not a shared theme alone'. Second defect: the closing seam is asserted as 'a different topic' while three byte-true chains cross it undisclosed -- “כסילים” is word-bound skeleton-identical at MT 7:4 and MT 7:5; the wisdom lexeme runs MT 7:4 to MT 7:5; and the laughter root stands at exactly 2 ch-7 verses, MT 7:3 and MT 7:6 (sweep: 2 verses), straddling this seam from inside the bracket into the next row. The bracket survives as skeleton-grade evidence, but it must be labelled, and re-cut it no longer outweighs the tokens crossing the closing seam. Third, this is a saying_cluster deviation inside the 7:1-14 single_saying-default sentence zone, where a cluster stands ONLY on byte-grounded cohesion named in the rationale: re-derived, every ADJACENT pair inside the span shares exactly ONE word-bound content token (MT 7:2/7:3 share only the opener marker; MT 7:3/7:4 share only the heart-token), i.e. cohesion thinner than the 2-shared-content-token threshold the gate names as a review trigger. Fair credit: the row does argue past the 7:1-8 tov-opener anaphora, the case the strategy names as the expected legitimate cluster, and it does so from bytes rather than by assertion.

Two defects. (1) Blended count object. The opener inventory counts VERSES whose FIRST skeleton token is the tov form -- re-derived independently as 12 book-wide and 7 in ch 7 (MT 7:1, 7:2, 7:3, 7:5, 7:8, 7:11, 7:18). MT 7:8 is the 5th and ONLY site in that list. Its second tov, “ט֥וֹב אֶֽרֶךְ ר֖וּחַ” (oshb:Eccl.7.8, byte tier), sits at token index 4 of 9 and is not verse-initial, so it cannot be an opener occurrence by the object's own definition; and '5th and 6th of 7' cannot both be drawn from a 7-member list that still contains MT 7:11 and MT 7:18. This is the semantic-class count discipline: a verse-object digit blended with a clause-object digit. (2) Disclosure asymmetry at the closing seam. The row discloses the Tier-4 WEB paragraph fold across MT 7:8 / 7:9 but asserts the verse 'shares no repeated phrase with ... the anger-admonition after it', while the spirit-token stands in exactly 2 ch-7 verses (sweep: 2 verses) -- MT 7:8 carrying it twice, “אֶֽרֶךְ ר֖וּחַ מִגְּבַהּ רֽוּחַ” (byte tier), and MT 7:9 carrying “בְּרֽוּחֲךָ֖” (oshb:Eccl.7.9, byte tier).
